text: Those stiff-necked in the face of reproofin an instant will be shattered beyond cure. [1]
When the just flourish, the people rejoice;but when the wicked rule, the people groan. [2] [AA]
Whoever loves wisdom gives joy to his father,but whoever consorts with harlots squanders his wealth.
By justice a king builds up the land;but one who raises taxes tears it down. [3]
Those who speak flattery to their neighborcast a net at their feet. [4]
The sin of the wicked is a trap,but the just run along joyfully. [AB]
The just care for the cause of the poor;the wicked do not understand such care. [5]
Scoffers enflame the city,but the wise calm the fury. [AC]
If a wise person disputes with a fool,there is railing and ridicule but no resolution.
The bloodthirsty hate the blameless,but the upright seek his life. [6]
Fools give vent to all their anger;but the wise, biding their time, control it. [AD]
If rulers listen to lying words,their servants all become wicked.
The poor and the oppressor meet: [AE]the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.
If a king is honestly for the rights of the poor,his throne stands firm forever. [AF]
The rod of correction gives wisdom,but uncontrolled youths disgrace their mothers. [AG]
When the wicked increase, crime increases;but the just will behold their downfall. [7]
Discipline your children, and they will bring you comfort,and give delight to your soul.
Without a vision the people lose restraint;but happy is the one who follows instruction. [8]
Not by words alone can servants be trained; [AH]for they understand but do not respond. [9]
Do you see someone hasty in speech? [AI]There is more hope for a fool!
If servants are pampered from childhoodthey will turn out to be stubborn.
The ill-tempered stir up strife,and the hotheaded cause many sins. [AJ]
Haughtiness brings humiliation,but the humble of spirit acquire honor. [10] [AK]
Partners of a thief hate themselves; [11]they hear the imprecation but do not testify.
Fear of others becomes a snare,but the one who trusts in the Lord is safe.
Many curry favor with a ruler,but it is from the Lord that one receives justice.
An abomination to the just, the evildoer;an abomination to the wicked, one whose way is straight.
